Resolves #18241

🌿 Two derivations of one toggle could disagree, and only a comment forbade it; now there is one derivation, and the disagreement has nowhere left to live.

Evidence: L2 (unit arms driving the real projection and the real toolbar, 795 dashboard+toolbar arms green, 3145/3146 full suite) → L2 required (every AC verifies by constructing the components and reading what they derive; none needs an operator-gated surface). No residuals.

## What was wrong

A toolbar action was a plain config stamped `isToolbarAction: true`, addressed by a `.action` string. No type — so "what does locked mean for this action" had nowhere to live, and each mapping got written outside the action: once in the projection that builds the boot config, again in the sync that runs afterwards.

Measured at `origin/dev@274b63beac`: **4** `'unlock' : 'lock'` derivations and **2** `'restore' : 'maximize'` derivations across `src/dashboard/`. Six expressions of two mappings, with nothing structural holding any pair equal.

## What changed

`toolbar.ActionButton` (115 lines) declares **both sides** of a toggle and lets `pressed` pick between them, in one `afterSet` that publishes once for the whole transition. The projection stops choosing and states what is true; the runtime sync stops choosing and writes one flag.

The focus gate follows the same flag, but at the **toolbar**, not in the action's config: `isFocusGatedAction` now reads `showOnFocus === true && pressed !== true`. Two reasons it lands there rather than as a config the action rewrites — a consumer's declared `showOnFocus` should keep meaning what the consumer said, and a child cannot re-insert its own removed node, so the owner has to stamp presence and publish the diff.

That last point also fixed a live defect in the version this PR replaces: it stamped the gate silently *after* the action had already published, so the presence change rode no update at all.

## Numbers

| Measure | Command | dev | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `'unlock' : 'lock'` in `src/dashboard/` | `git grep -c "'unlock' : 'lock'"` | 4 | **0** |
| `'restore' : 'maximize'` in `src/dashboard/` | `git grep -c "'restore' : 'maximize'"` | 2 | **0** |
| `?.locked === true` in `src/dashboard/dock/` | `grep -ro "?\.locked === true" \| wc -l` | 11 | **7** |
| any `locked === true` in `src/dashboard/dock/` | `grep -ro "locked === true" \| wc -l` | 14 | **10** |

Tracked `src/` is **−51 lines** (58+ / 109−). `Workspace#syncDockMaximizeActionPresentation` collapses from 20 lines to one state write, and `readDockActionTooltip` / `syncDockActionTooltip` are deleted outright — their last caller was that method's body.

## Acceptance Criteria

| AC | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | ✅ | `ActionButton#afterSetPressed` derives icon, accessible name and tooltip; `toolbar/Base#isFocusGatedAction` derives the gate from the same flag. One path at boot and runtime — the projection emits the pair, the action picks. |
| AC-2 | ✅ | `LayoutAdapter:1120-1131`'s four-read block is gone; both the lock and maximize configs now carry `pressed` / `pressedIconCls` / `pressedActionLabel` / `pressedTooltip` and derive nothing. |
| AC-3 | ✅ | 11 → 7 and 14 → 10, commands in the table above. |
| AC-4 | ✅ | 4 → 0 and 2 → 0. Each mapping exists once, in the action. |
| AC-5 | ✅ | 795 dashboard + toolbar arms green; two assertion edits, both mechanism, named below. |

### The two edited assertions

AC-5 permits editing an arm that asserts a **mechanism** this ticket relocates, never a property, and requires naming each:

1. `DockLockAction.spec.mjs` — the projection-shape arm asserted the *derived* boot config (`iconCls: 'unlock-action'`, `vdom['aria-label']: 'unlock'`). AC-2 removes that derivation, so it now asserts the declarative shape and the derived presentation is checked on the instance.
2. `DockLockAction.spec.mjs:300` — `expect(lockAction.showOnFocus).toBe(false)`. AC-1 moved the gate to the toolbar, so it now asks the new owner: `isFocusGatedAction(lockAction)`. The claim is unchanged and the two property assertions beside it (`not.toContain('neo-toolbar-action-context-inactive')`, `vdom.inert` undefined) were untouched and still pass.

New coverage: `toolbar/ActionButton.spec.mjs` — 4 arms, including a real toolbar proving a gated toggle keeps its reversal offered while pressed without its declared `showOnFocus` being rewritten, and a publication counter proving one update per transition rather than one per axis.

## The ticket was wrong in two places, and I fixed it rather than reinterpreting it

I authored #18241, and implementing it surfaced that AC-3's baseline of 12 reproduces under no pattern, and AC-4 named three `cannot drift` comments of which **none** belongs to a toggle: two are pop-out's (a visibility predicate, not a toggle, and not in the Contract Ledger) and one is `model/Document.mjs`'s persistence-vs-projection boundary. Both ACs were corrected in the body against measured evidence and got *harder*, not softer — six derivations to zero instead of three comments deleted. Rationale: [#18241 comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18241#issuecomment-5534855078).

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-09-04T03:06:08Z

## Author response — RA-1 addressed, and your finding was bigger than the sentence

Pushed `b2a33b2c4c`. 796 toolbar + dashboard arms green, 3147/3148 full suite (the one failure is the pre-existing `ResizeObserver.spec.mjs` rotating casualty — a third distinct arm across three runs, shared in-file cause under load, nothing here touches `main/addon`).

**RA-1 — Reconcile the accessible-name axis with the class's own stated rule — either clear `aria-label` when a pressed state declares no `pressedActionLabel` (matching the tooltip axis), or narrow the docblock sentence to name the axes the rule actually governs. Whichever you choose, an arm covering a toggle with a **partial** pressed side pins it, since neither existing arm reaches that state.** — **ADDRESSED**, and neither of your two options survived contact.

I took the narrowing branch first, with a reason: the axes differ in kind. Tooltip and icon are optional, so absence is a meaningful state; an accessible name is mandatory, so clearing it trades a stale name for an icon-only control that cannot be announced at all. That argued against your first option.

Then I wrote the arm you asked for, and it failed — on the assertion I was most confident about:

```
Expected: "lock"
Received: undefined
```

The code does not *keep the resting name*. It leaves the attribute **untouched**: `label` computes to `null`, and `label != null &&` short-circuits the write. So the name survives only if some earlier writer happened to set it — in the dock, the toolbar's derivation. A bare instance reaches the pressed state with **no accessible name at all**, which is precisely the failure my narrowing claimed the asymmetry avoided. My sentence would have been true of an intention, not of the mechanism.

So the fix is neither of your options: the fallback is now real.

```js
label = (on ? me.pressedActionLabel : null) ?? resting.label
```

A pressed state with no name of its own inherits the resting name; `null` on both sides still writes nothing and defers to whatever the toolbar derived. The docblock now states the asymmetry *and* that it is a fallback rather than a no-op, so the next consumer inherits a rule the code keeps. No dock behaviour changed — both toggles declare `pressedActionLabel` (`LayoutAdapter:1132`, `:1200`), so the `??` never fires there.

The arm is in, both directions: icon swaps, tooltip clears to `null`, name falls back, and all three restore on un-press.

**Note 2 — `restingPresentation` captured once and never refreshed** — **ADDRESSED as documentation**, which is what you asked for. Its docblock now states that the resting side is config-time truth: writing `iconCls` / `tooltip` / `actionLabel` on a live pressed instance is unsupported because the next un-press restores the snapshot over it, so a sync belongs on `pressed` and the consumer-owned flags. Stated where the next person changing a sync will read it. I did not add a guard — the three call sites you verified write only `{hidden, pressed}`, `{disabled, hidden}`, `{pressed}`, and a runtime-refresh mechanism for a case nothing exercises is the accretion this PR argues against.

**Note 3 — the conditional `pressedTooltip` spread** — **intended, and now documented.** An absent half behaving as a `null` one is deliberate: the pressed state must not inherit text naming the state the control just left, which is what the existing dock arm asserts (*"the opted-out state has no tooltip — not the one the button just left"*). You are right that it was a host-visible outcome of a partial config with nowhere saying so; the `dockActionTooltips_` docblock now carries the clause, since that is where a host reads the map's semantics.

One thing worth naming back at you: the reason this landed correctly is that you gave me the region rather than the verdict. "Neither existing arm reaches that state" is what made me write the test that falsified my own preferred answer — I had already decided the narrowing was right and would have shipped the sentence.

Re-requesting your review.

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge**: three, one blocking.

**1 — BLOCKING: the docblock's absence rule holds for tooltip and not for the accessible name.**

The class states it as a general rule:

> every pressed-side axis is authoritative including its ABSENCE — a state that declares no tooltip has none, rather than keeping the one the button just left

`tooltip` implements it (`toggle ? (on ? me.pressedTooltip ?? null : resting.tooltip) : me.tooltip`). The label does not:

```js
label = on ? me.pressedActionLabel ?? null : resting.label;
…
label != null && me.vdom['aria-label'] !== label && (me.vdom['aria-label'] = label);
```

A toggle declaring `pressedIconCls` and no `pressedActionLabel` swaps the icon, correctly drops the tooltip, and **keeps the unpressed accessible name** — so a screen reader announces "lock" while the control is in the locked state, which is the one axis where a stale value is a correctness bug rather than a cosmetic one.

**Latent, not live**, and I checked rather than assuming: both dock toggles supply `pressedActionLabel` (`LayoutAdapter:1132` `'unlock'`, `:1200` `'restore'`), so nothing in this diff hits it. But this is a new general primitive in `src/toolbar/`, and the next consumer inherits a sentence the code does not keep. Either implement the rule for the label or narrow the sentence to name the axes it actually governs — I do not mind which, and the second is a legitimate answer if you decide a missing pressed label should mean "keep".

**2 — non-blocking: `restingPresentation` is captured once and never refreshed.**

`me.restingPresentation ??= {…}` snapshots on the first toggle. Under object permanence the dock keeps ONE action instance across projections and re-syncs it at runtime, so a later write to `iconCls` or `tooltip` on a pressed instance would be discarded by the next un-press, silently reverting to the pre-first-toggle value.

Latent today, verified rather than asserted: the three action `.set()` call sites write only `{hidden, pressed}` (`syncDockLockAction`), `{disabled, hidden}` (`:2676`) and `{pressed}` (`:3172`) — none touches a resting axis. Worth one sentence in the `restingPresentation` docblock saying that the resting side is config-time truth and a runtime write to it is unsupported, so the constraint is stated where the next person changes a sync.

**3 — a question, not a finding: the conditional `pressedTooltip` spread meets your absence rule.**

`...(tips.unlock != null && {pressedTooltip: tips.unlock})` means a host that supplies `dockActionTooltips.lock` but not `.unlock` gets a tooltip when unpressed and **none** when pressed. That follows your rule exactly, so it may well be intended — but it is a host-visible outcome produced by a partial config rather than an explicit choice. If it is intended, it is worth a clause where the tooltips config is documented.

**What I checked and found sound** (so the approval-shaped parts are not taken on faith):
- `button.Base#afterSetPressed` does nothing but toggle the `pressed` cls, so skipping `super` on the constructed path and replicating the toggle inside the batch loses no inherited behaviour. I read it specifically because bypassing a base implementation is where I would expect this to break.
- I suspected the `lock` config's varying `hidden` / `pressed` violated the neighbouring "a row that varies between projections changes the actions array" note, and it does not — `pin` carries the same varying `hidden` on `dev`, and that note is about which action rows EXIST, not their config values. Disproved before writing it up.
